An imported run is a log from your real robot, not from this simulator.
  1. Copy FTCKesselRunLog.java out of spike/src/org/firstinspires/ftc/teamcode/ into your own TeamCode, beside your OpModes. It needs nothing but the SDK.
  2. In the autonomous you want to record: FTCKesselRunLog log = new FTCKesselRunLog(hardwareMap, "BlueFarAuto"); then log.markStart() after waitForStart(), log.tick(getRuntime()) once a loop, and log.close().
  3. Run it once on a real field, from a tile you can identify, then pull the .pflog off the Robot Controller and open it with Import a run.

The recorded path is drawn in magenta beside the simulated one, so you can see where the two stopped agreeing rather than only that they did. docs/RECORDING-A-RUN.md is the long version.

This is a different thing from Record and Replay above, which tape what you do on the sticks here and play it back into this simulator.

Two controllers drive GP1 and GP2
          directly, in the order the browser reports them. The keyboard drives whichever
          gamepad is selected, so one person at a laptop can still reach both halves of the
          robot. The deck turns red when the robot is against a wall.

        

      

    



  


  

    Start it with --project <your TeamCode source root> and it compiles and runs the
    code in your actual repository — edit in Android Studio, save, and it rebuilds here.
    Pick an OpMode, press INIT, then Start, and drive. Plug in a controller and it is picked
    up automatically; otherwise use WASD to drive and
    QE to turn. The deck turns red when the robot is against a wall.
    Everything you are driving is FIRST's own SDK running on a JVM — the browser only sends stick
    positions and draws what comes back.
    Not modelled yet: battery sag, and collision response beyond stopping at the wall.
